timeline.title: Indus Valley Civilization
timeline.description: The mature urban phase of the Indus Valley Civilization developed major cities, planned streets, drainage systems, craft production and long-distance trade.
timeline.importance: One of the world's earliest major urban civilizations.

timeline.title: Unification of Ancient Egypt
timeline.description: The political unification of Upper and Lower Egypt marked the beginning of the early dynastic period of ancient Egyptian civilization.
timeline.importance: Established one of the longest-lasting civilizations of the ancient world.

timeline.title: Rise of Sumerian Cities
timeline.description: Sumerian city-states such as Uruk, Ur and Lagash became important centers of urban life, writing, administration and trade.
timeline.importance: Mesopotamia became one of the earliest centers of cities and writing.

timeline.title: Early Writing Systems
timeline.description: Cuneiform developed in Mesopotamia as a system for recording economic, administrative and later literary information.
timeline.importance: Writing transformed record keeping, administration and the transmission of knowledge.

timeline.title: Great Pyramid of Giza
timeline.description: The Great Pyramid was constructed during Egypt's Fourth Dynasty and became the largest of the Giza pyramids.
timeline.importance: One of the most famous surviving monuments of the ancient world.

timeline.title: Code of Hammurabi
timeline.description: The Code of Hammurabi is an ancient Babylonian collection of laws associated with King Hammurabi.
timeline.importance: An important surviving example of an ancient written legal tradition.

timeline.title: Vedic Period
timeline.description: The Vedic period saw the development and transmission of Vedic traditions, Sanskrit literature and changing social and political institutions.
timeline.importance: A foundational period in the development of ancient Indian culture and intellectual traditions.

timeline.title: Unification of China
timeline.description: Qin Shi Huang unified several major Chinese states and established the Qin imperial dynasty.
timeline.importance: Created the first centralized imperial state that unified much of the Chinese heartland.

timeline.title: Rise of the Mauryan Empire
timeline.description: Chandragupta Maurya established the Mauryan Empire, which became one of the largest political formations in ancient South Asia.
timeline.importance: Marked a major period of political consolidation in ancient Indian history.

timeline.title: Reign of Emperor Ashoka
timeline.description: Ashoka became one of the most prominent Mauryan rulers. His inscriptions provide important evidence about his policies and ideas.
timeline.importance: Ashoka's reign is a major chapter in ancient Indian political and cultural history.

timeline.title: Classical Athens
timeline.description: Classical Athens became a major center of philosophy, drama, art, architecture and political experimentation.
timeline.importance: Its intellectual and artistic traditions had a lasting influence on world history.

timeline.title: Alexander the Great Begins His Reign
timeline.description: Alexander became king of Macedon and later established a vast empire stretching from Greece toward Egypt and parts of Asia.
timeline.importance: His campaigns accelerated cultural interactions across a large part of the ancient world.

timeline.title: Roman Republic
timeline.description: Rome traditionally dates the establishment of its Republic to 509 BCE after the end of its monarchy.
timeline.importance: The Roman Republic developed institutions that influenced later Roman government and political thought.

timeline.title: Beginning of the Roman Empire
timeline.description: Octavian became Augustus, traditionally marking the beginning of the Roman imperial period.
timeline.importance: The Roman Empire became one of the most influential political and cultural systems of antiquity.

timeline.title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius
timeline.description: Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii and nearby settlements under volcanic material.
timeline.importance: The destruction preserved buildings, objects and evidence of everyday Roman life.

timeline.title: Rise of the Gupta Empire
timeline.description: The Gupta dynasty established a powerful kingdom in northern India and presided over important developments in science, mathematics, literature and art.
timeline.importance: The Gupta period is often remembered as an important era of classical Indian culture.

timeline.title: Constantinople Becomes Imperial Capital
timeline.description: Constantine established Constantinople as a major imperial capital on the site of Byzantium.
timeline.importance: The city later became the center of the Byzantine Empire.

timeline.title: Rise of the Khmer Empire
timeline.description: The Khmer Empire developed into a major Southeast Asian power and created an extensive network of temples and water-management systems.
timeline.importance: Khmer architecture and urban planning left a major cultural legacy.

timeline.title: Magna Carta
timeline.description: King John accepted Magna Carta at Runnymede in 1215.
timeline.importance: It became an important historical document in the development of ideas about law and limits on government power.

timeline.title: Rise of the Mongol Empire
timeline.description: Temüjin was proclaimed Genghis Khan and began the political consolidation that led to the Mongol Empire.
timeline.importance: The Mongol Empire became the largest contiguous land empire in recorded history.

timeline.title: Foundation of Vijayanagara
timeline.description: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in southern India and later became a major political and cultural center.
timeline.importance: Its capital region at Hampi contains major examples of South Indian architecture and urban heritage.

timeline.title: Gutenberg Printing Revolution
timeline.description: Johannes Gutenberg's printing technology helped make the large-scale production of books more practical in Europe.
timeline.importance: Printing transformed the spread of knowledge, education and ideas.

timeline.title: Fall of Constantinople
timeline.description: Ottoman forces under Mehmed II captured Constantinople in 1453.
timeline.importance: The event marked the end of the Byzantine Empire and a major transition in Eurasian history.

timeline.title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
timeline.description: Christopher Columbus's 1492 expedition reached islands in the Caribbean, beginning a new phase of sustained contact between Europe and the Americas.
timeline.importance: The voyages contributed to major demographic, economic, political and cultural changes across the Atlantic world.

timeline.title: European Renaissance
timeline.description: The Renaissance was a broad cultural movement associated with renewed interest in classical learning, art, literature and scientific inquiry.
timeline.importance: It profoundly influenced European art, education and intellectual history.

timeline.title: Beginning of the Mughal Empire
timeline.description: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat and established Mughal rule in northern India.
timeline.importance: The Mughal Empire became one of the major imperial powers in South Asian history.

timeline.title: Protestant Reformation
timeline.description: Martin Luther's challenge to aspects of church practice became a major catalyst for the Protestant Reformation.
timeline.importance: The Reformation transformed European religious, political and social history.

timeline.title: Scientific Revolution
timeline.description: European scholars developed new approaches to observation, experimentation and mathematical description of nature.
timeline.importance: The movement helped shape modern scientific methods and institutions.

timeline.title: Tokugawa Shogunate
timeline.description: Tokugawa Ieyasu established the Tokugawa shogunate, which governed Japan for more than two centuries.
timeline.importance: The period brought political stability and major developments in Japanese society and culture.

timeline.title: Industrial Revolution
timeline.description: Mechanized production, new energy systems, factories and transportation transformed economic and social life.
timeline.importance: The Industrial Revolution reshaped the modern global economy and urban society.

timeline.title: United States Declaration of Independence
timeline.description: The Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776.
timeline.importance: The declaration became a foundational document of the United States.

timeline.title: French Revolution
timeline.description: The French Revolution began a period of profound political and social transformation in France.
timeline.importance: Its ideas and political consequences influenced modern concepts of citizenship, government and rights.

timeline.title: Haitian Revolution
timeline.description: The Haitian Revolution was a successful revolutionary struggle that led to the establishment of independent Haiti.
timeline.importance: It was a major event in Atlantic history and the history of emancipation.

timeline.title: Napoleon Becomes Emperor
timeline.description: Napoleon Bonaparte was crowned Emperor of the French in 1804.
timeline.importance: Napoleonic rule transformed European politics, warfare and law.

timeline.title: Latin American Independence Movements
timeline.description: A series of independence movements transformed Spanish and Portuguese colonial rule across much of Latin America.
timeline.importance: These movements created numerous independent states in the Americas.

timeline.title: Indian Rebellion of 1857
timeline.description: A major uprising against East India Company rule began in northern and central parts of India in 1857.
timeline.importance: The rebellion led to major changes in the structure of British rule in India.

timeline.title: German Unification
timeline.description: The German Empire was proclaimed in 1871 following a series of political and military developments led by Prussia.
timeline.importance: German unification changed the political balance of Europe.

timeline.title: Telephone Patent Era
timeline.description: Alexander Graham Bell received a U.S. patent for an apparatus for transmitting vocal or other sounds telegraphically.
timeline.importance: Telephone technology transformed long-distance communication.

timeline.title: World War I
timeline.description: World War I was a global conflict involving major powers and their allies.
timeline.importance: The war caused enormous human and political changes and reshaped the international order.

timeline.title: Indian Independence Movement
timeline.description: Indian political and social movements campaigned for independence from British rule through diverse strategies and organizations.
timeline.importance: The movement culminated in the independence of India in 1947.

timeline.title: World War II
timeline.description: World War II was a global conflict fought across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Pacific.
timeline.importance: The war profoundly changed global politics, borders, economies and international institutions.

timeline.title: United Nations Established
timeline.description: The United Nations was established in 1945 following the Second World War.
timeline.importance: It became a central international organization for diplomacy, peace and cooperation.

timeline.title: Indian Independence
timeline.description: India became independent from British rule on August 15, 1947.
timeline.importance: Indian independence was a major event in the history of decolonization.

timeline.title: India Becomes a Republic
timeline.description: The Constitution of India came into effect on January 26, 1950, establishing India as a republic.
timeline.importance: It established the constitutional framework of the Republic of India.

timeline.title: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
timeline.description: NASA's Apollo 11 mission landed humans on the Moon, with Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walking on the lunar surface.
timeline.importance: It marked a landmark achievement in human space exploration.

timeline.title: Rise of the Internet
timeline.description: Computer networking developed into the global Internet, followed by the rapid expansion of the World Wide Web.
timeline.importance: The Internet transformed communication, information access, education, commerce and culture.

timeline.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
timeline.description: The Berlin Wall opened in November 1989, becoming a major symbol of the end of the Cold War division in Europe.
timeline.importance: The event preceded German reunification and major changes in European politics.

timeline.title: German Reunification
timeline.description: East and West Germany were reunified on October 3, 1990.
timeline.importance: Reunification became a major turning point in modern European history.

timeline.title: World Wide Web Becomes Public
timeline.description: The World Wide Web was developed by Tim Berners-Lee and became publicly accessible in the early 1990s.
timeline.importance: The Web became one of the most important systems for sharing information over the Internet.

timeline.title: Global Digital Era
timeline.description: Smartphones, cloud computing, social platforms, digital services and artificial intelligence increasingly transformed everyday life.
timeline.importance: Digital technologies became central to communication, education, business and global culture.
